questions.question: Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All squirrels are lizards. All lizards are goose. Conclusions: I. Some squirrels are not goose. II. Some lizards are squirrels. III. Some goose are squirrels.
questions.questionHtml:
Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All squirrels are lizards.

All lizards are goose.

Conclusions:

I. Some squirrels are not goose.

II. Some lizards are squirrels.

III. Some goose are squirrels.

options.text: Conclusions I, II and III follow
options.html: Conclusions I, II and III follow

questions.solution:
Statement I: All squirrels are lizards.

Statement II: All lizards are goose.

Conclusion:

I: Some squirrels are not goose → False.

II: Some lizards are squirrels → True.

III: Some goose are squirrels → True.

Hence, “Conclusion II and III” follows.

questions.solution:

In case of 16 : 240,

Similarly,

= 6 : 30

Hence, “30” is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 27 ÷ 3 – 18 + 3 × 2 = 18
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

27 ÷ 3 – 18 + 3 × 2 = 18
questions.solution:
Given Equation: 27 ÷ 3 – 18 + 3 × 2 = 18

Let’s check each option,

1) Interchanging ÷ and ×

Equation will become: - 27 × 3 – 18 + 3 ÷ 2

81 – 18 + 1.5 ≠ 18

2) Interchanging × and +

Equation will become: - 27 ÷ 3 – 18 × 3 + 2

9 – 54 + 2 ≠ 18

3) Interchanging + and –

Equation will become: - 27 ÷ 3 + 18 - 3 × 2

8 + 18 – 6 ≠ 18

4) Interchanging + and ÷

Equation will become: - 27 + 3 – 18 ÷ 3 × 2

27 + 3 – 6 × 2

30 – 12 = 18

Thus, interchanging “+ and ÷” we get the correct answer.

questions.question: Three different positions of the same dice are shown below. Which symbol is on the face opposite the face showing ‘*’?
questions.questionHtml: Three different positions of the same dice are shown below. Which symbol is on the face opposite the face showing ‘*’?
questions.solution:
The symbol # appears in 2 dice position i.e. 1st and 2nd from which it is evident that $, &, + and * are adjacent to it and cannot be opposite to #. From this we can conclude that # will face opposite to %.

Similarly, + appears in 2 dice positions i.e. 2nd and 3rd from which it is evident that #, *, &, % are adjacent to it and cannot be opposite to +. So, + will face opposite to $.

From the above conclusions we can conclude that * and & will face each other.

Hence, “&” is the correct answer.

questions.question: The sum of the current ages of Natasha and Krishna is 50 years. 10 years ago, Krishna was twice as old as Natasha. What is Krishna’s current age?
questions.questionHtml: The sum of the current ages of Natasha and Krishna is 50 years. 10 years ago, Krishna was twice as old as Natasha. What is Krishna’s current age?
questions.solution:
Let the age of Natasha be” x” and age of Krishna be “y”.

As per statement given in question:

x + y = 50     ...(i) and

Ten years ago:

Natasha = x -10 years old

Krishna = y -10 years old

→ y – 10 = 2(x – 10)

→ 2x –y = 20 – 10     ...(ii)

From both the equations (i) and (ii)

→ 2x + 2y = 100

→ 2x – y = 10

→ 3y = 90 → y = 30

And x = 20.

Hence, Krishna’s age is 30 years.

questions.question: A + B means ‘A is the mother of B’ A - B means ‘A is the father of B’ A × B means ‘A is the sister of B’ A ÷ B means ‘A is the daughter of B’ If P + R × T – Q ÷ S + U, then how is S related to T?
questions.questionHtml:
A + B means ‘A is the mother of B’

A - B means ‘A is the father of B’

A × B means ‘A is the sister of B’

A ÷ B means ‘A is the daughter of B’

If P + R × T – Q ÷ S + U, then how is S related to T?
questions.solution:
According to the question, P + R × T – Q ÷ S + U can be decoded as P is mother of R, R is sister of T, T is father of Q, Q is daughter of S, S is mother of U.

From the above arrangement, S is wife of T.

Hence, “Wife” is the correct answer.

questions.question: The Indus Water Treaty was signed between India and ______.
questions.questionHtml: The Indus Water Treaty was signed between India and ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pakistan.

Key Points

  • The Indus Water Treaty (IWT) is a water-distribution treaty between India and Pakistan which was signed on September 19, 1960.
  • The treaty was signed by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Pakistan’s President Ayub Khan.
  • The treaty deals with river Indus and its five tributaries.

These are divided into two categories - 
Eastern Rivers:

  • Sutlej
  • Beas
  • Ravi

Western Rivers:

  • Jhelum
  • Chenab
  • Indus
     

According to the treaty, all the water of the eastern rivers shall be available for unrestricted use in India, and India must allow unrestricted flow of water from the western rivers to Pakistan.

questions.solution:
• Indian king Rajendra Chola-I used naval powers to conquer parts of Eastasia.
  • He defeated Sri Vijaya or the Kadaram kingdom in East Asia and bore the title Kadaramkonda.

questions.question: Night Blindness is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin _______.
questions.questionHtml: Night Blindness is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin _______.
questions.solution:

  • Xerophthalmia, Keratomalacia, and complete blindness can also occur since vitamin A has a major role in phototransduction.

questions.question: When was the Constitution of Pakistan enforced?

questions.solution:
The National Assembly of Pakistan passed it's Constitution on 10th April, 1973.

The President of the constituent Assembly authenticated it on 12th April 1973 and the Assembly published the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

After partitioned from India, Pakistan was declared as an Islamic Republic and it was made mandatory that only a Muslim could become the President of the country.

questions.question: The radii of the two circular faces of the frustum of a cone of height 14 cm are 5 cm and 2 cm. What is its volume in cm3? (π = 22/7)
questions.questionHtml: The radii of the two circular faces of the frustum of a cone of height 14 cm are 5 cm and 2 cm. What is its volume in cm3? (π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Radii of two circular faces of the frustum of a cone are 5 cm and 2 cm

Height of the circular frustum of cone H = 14 cm

As we know,

Volume of the frustum of cone = 1/3 × π [R2 + r2 + Rr] 14

⇒ 1/3 × 22/7 × [52 + 22 + 5 × 2] × 14

⇒ 22/3 × [25 + 4 + 10] × 2

⇒ 22/3 × 39 × 2

⇒ 572

questions.questionHtml: A train without stoppage travels with an average speed of 80 km/h and with stoppage, it travels with an average speed of 72 km/h. For how many minutes does the train stop on an average per hour?
questions.solution:
Without stoppage average speed = 80 km/h

With stoppages average speed = 72 km/h

As we know,

Time of rest per hour equal to the difference in average speed divided by the speed without stoppage.

Required time = [(80 – 72)/80] × 60 = 6

So, A train stops on an average 6 minute/hr

questions.question: The price of sugar is increased by 21%. A person wants to increase his expenditure by 12% only. By what percent, correct to one decimal place, should be reduce his consumption?
questions.questionHtml: The price of sugar is increased by 21%. A person wants to increase his expenditure by 12% only. By what percent, correct to one decimal place, should be reduce his consumption?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Let the initial price of sugar be 100x

Price of sugar after increased = 100x × [121 / 100] = 121x

Person wants his expenditure increase by 12% only,

So, his expenditure should be = 100x × [112 / 100] = 112x

Required percentage = [(121x – 112x) / 121x] × 100 = 7.43% ≈ 7.4%

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, AB is the diameter and CD is a chord such that ABCD is a trapezium. If ∠BAC = 24°, then ∠CAD is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with centre O, AB is the diameter and CD is a chord such that ABCD is a trapezium. If ∠BAC = 24°, then ∠CAD is equal to∶
questions.solution:
Given, ∠BAC = 24°

⇒ ∠ACB = 90° [Angle in a semicircle is 90]

In ΔACB

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠CBA + ∠BAC = 180°

⇒ ∠CBA = 180° – 90° – 24° = 66°

⇒ ∠BDC = ∠CAB = 24° [Alternate interior angle]

⇒ ∠DCA = ∠ABD = 24° and ∠CAD = ∠DBC

∵ Two inscribed angles forming the same arc or forming two equal arcs are equal.

⇒ ∠CBA = ∠DBC + ∠ABD

⇒ 66° = ∠DBC + 24°

⇒ ∠DBC = 66° – 24° = 42°

⇒ ∠CAD = ∠DBC = 42°

questions.question: A is 50% more efficient than B and C is 40% less efficient than B. Working together, they can complete a task in 10 days. In how many days will A alone complete 150% of that task?
questions.questionHtml: A is 50% more efficient than B and C is 40% less efficient than B. Working together, they can complete a task in 10 days. In how many days will A alone complete 150% of that task?
questions.solution:
Let the efficiency of B be 100.

Efficiency of A will be = 100 × [150/100] = 150

Efficiency of C will be = 100 × [60/100] = 60

Efficiency ratio of A, B and C = 150 ∶ 100 ∶ 60 = 15 ∶ 10 ∶ 6

Total work = (15 + 10 + 6) × 10 = 310

150% of total work = 310 × [150/100] = 465

150% of total work A will complete in = 465/15 = 31 days

questions.question: ΔABC ∼ ΔQPR and AB = 8 cm, BC = 12 cm and AC = 6 cm. If ar(ΔABC) ∶ ar(ΔPQR) = 16 ∶ 25, then RQ is equal to
questions.questionHtml: ΔABC ∼ ΔQPR and AB = 8 cm, BC = 12 cm and AC = 6 cm. If ar(ΔABC) ∶ ar(ΔPQR) = 16 ∶ 25, then RQ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given:

AB = 8 cm

BC = 12 cm

AC = 6 cm

ar(ΔABC)/ar(ΔPQR) = 16/25

Concept used:

In similar triangles, the ratio of their areas is the square of the ratio of their sides.

Calculation:

According to the question,

Let QR = x (since QR corresponds to AC in ΔABC)

(ar(ΔABC)/ar(ΔPQR)) = (AC/QR)2

⇒ (16/25) = (6/x)2

⇒ 4/5 = 6/x

⇒ x = 30/4 = 7.5 cm

 RQ = 7.5 cm

∴ RQ is equal to 7.5 cm.

questions.question: Two articles are sold for Rs. 2508 each. On one, there is a gain of 14% and on the other, there is a loss of 12%. What is the overall gain or loss percent to nearest one decimal place?
questions.questionHtml: Two articles are sold for Rs. 2508 each. On one, there is a gain of 14% and on the other, there is a loss of 12%. What is the overall gain or loss percent to nearest one decimal place?
questions.solution:
SP of each article = Rs. 2508

CP of first article = 2508 × [100/114] = 2,200

CP of second article = 2508 × [100/88] = 2,850

Total SP of both article = 2508 × 2 = 5,016

Total CP of both article = 2,200 + 2,850 = 5,050

Total loss = 5,050 – 5,016 = 34

Loss percentage = [34/5,050] × 100 = 0.673% = 0.7% (approx)

questions.question: If \(\sqrt{x}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}=\sqrt{7},\) then \({{x}^{3}}+\frac{1}{{{x}^{3}}}\) is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: If \(\sqrt{x}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}=\sqrt{7},\) then \({{x}^{3}}+\frac{1}{{{x}^{3}}}\) is equal to∶
questions.solution:
As we know,

⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = x2 + 1/x2 + 2

Given, √x + 1/√x = √7

⇒ (√x + 1/√x)2 = (√x)2 + (1/√x)2 + 2

⇒ √72 = x + 1/x + 2

⇒ x + 1/x = 7 – 2 = 5

As we know,

⇒ (x + 1/x)3 = x3 + 1/x3 + 3(x + 1/x)

⇒ 53 = x3 + 1/x3 + 3 × 5

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = 125 – 15 = 110

questions.question: Find the value of 5.8 + (7.4 ÷ 3.7 × 5) – 6 × 2 ÷ 2.5
questions.questionHtml: Find the value of 5.8 + (7.4 ÷ 3.7 × 5) – 6 × 2 ÷ 2.5
questions.solution:
Follow BODMAS rule to solve this question, as per the order given below∶
Step-1∶ Parts of an equation enclosed in 'Brackets' must be solved first, and in the bracket,
Step-2∶ Any mathematical 'Of' or 'Exponent' must be solved next,
Step-3∶ Next, the parts of the equation that contain 'Division' and 'Multiplication' are calculated,
Step-4∶ Last but not least, the parts of the equation that contain 'Addition' and 'Subtraction' should be calculated.     

⇒ 5.8 + (7.4 ÷ 3.7 × 5) – 6 × 2 ÷ 2.5

⇒ 5.8 + (2 × 5) – 6 × 0.8

⇒ 5.8 + 10 – 4.8

⇒ 11

questions.question: If a + b + c = 4 and ab + bc + ca = 2, then a 3 + b 3 + c 3 – 3abc is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: If a + b + c = 4 and ab + bc + ca = 2, then a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup> + c<sup>3</sup> – 3abc is equal to∶
questions.solution:
Given:

a + b + c = 4 and ab + bc + ca = 2

Formula used:

a3 + b3 + c3 – 3abc = (a + b + c)(a2 + b2 + c2 - ab - bc - ca)

(a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca

Calculation:

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 – 3abc = (a + b +c) [(a + b + c)2 – 3(ab + bc + ca)]

⇒ 4 [42 – 3 × 2]

⇒ 4 (16 – 6)

⇒ 4 × 10

⇒ 40

Additional Informationa3 + b3 + c3 – 3abc = (a + b + c)(a2 + b2 + c2 - ab - bc - ca)

a2 + b2 + c2 = (a + b + c)2 - 2(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ (a + b + c){(a + b + c)2 - 2(ab + bc + ca) - (ab + bc + ca)}

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 – 3abc = (a + b +c) [(a + b + c)2 – 3(ab + bc + ca)]

questions.question: For what value of x is the seven digit number 46393x8 divisible by 11?
questions.questionHtml: For what value of x is the seven digit number 46393x8 divisible by 11?
questions.solution:
As we know,

Divisibility law of 11∶ If the difference of the alternating sum of digits of the number is a multiple of 11 (e.g. 2343 is divisible by 11 because 2 - 3 + 4 - 3 = 0, which is a multiple of 11).

⇒ 46393x8 divisible by 11 if x = 3

Or

⇒ 4 – 6 + 3 – 9 + 3 – x + 8 = 0

⇒ x = 18 – 15 = 3

questions.question: In a class of 50 students, 46% are girls and the remaining are boys. The average of the boys’ marks is 58 and that of the girls is 62. What are the average marks of the whole class?
questions.questionHtml: In a class of 50 students, 46% are girls and the remaining are boys. The average of the boys’ marks is 58 and that of the girls is 62. What are the average marks of the whole class?
questions.solution:
Number of girls in class = 50 × 46/100 = 23

Number of boys in class = 50 – 23 = 27

Average marks of girls = 62

Sum of marks of girls = 62 × 23 = 1426

Average marks of boys = 58

Sum of marks of boys = 58 × 27 = 1566

Total sum of marks of all class = 1426 + 1566 = 2992

Average marks of whole class = 2992/50 = 59.84

questions.question: The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. A. The first of these states that the only way to have a friend is to be one. B. Like all relationships, it is also governed by some well-defined principles. C. Friendship is one of the most coveted relationships on earth. D. Thus, one must be reliable as a friend to expect reliability in others.
questions.questionHtml:
The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

A. The first of these states that the only way to have a friend is to be one.

B. Like all relationships, it is also governed by some well-defined principles.

C. Friendship is one of the most coveted relationships on earth.

D. Thus, one must be reliable as a friend to expect reliability in others.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is CBAD

Key Points

  • The given sentence is an example of a Sentence Jumble. 
  • The first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, the starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
  • Part C will be the first sentence because it an independent general statement. It establishes the theme for the passage.
  • Part B will be the next in sequence. It has the pronoun 'it', referring back to 'friendship'.
  • Part A will be the next in sequence. It mentions the first principle the friendship is governed.
  • Part D is the conclusive statement, so should be kept at the last.


The sequence in which sentences are arranged is: Friendship is one of the most coveted relationships on earth. Like all relationships, it is also governed by some well-defined principles. The first of these states that the only way to have a friend is to be one. Thus, one must be reliable as a friend to expect reliability in others.

questions.question: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. That which cannot be satisfied
questions.questionHtml:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.

That which cannot be satisfied
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Insatiable".Key Points

  • The word that means "that which cannot be satisfied" is "insatiable."
  • Insatiable: This word refers to an intense or unquenchable desire or appetite that cannot be satisfied. It implies a constant craving or longing for more and is often used to describe someone who has an insatiable hunger or thirst for something, whether it be food, success, knowledge, or experiences.
    • Example: Despite having a full meal, his insatiable appetite drove him to raid the fridge for more snacks.
  • Now, let's look at the other options:
  • Impossible: This word refers to something that cannot be done, achieved, or realized. It indicates that a particular action, event, or outcome is not possible or cannot happen.
    • Example: It is impossible to fly without the assistance of an aircraft or wings.
  • Incredible: This word means something that is hard to believe, astonishing, or extraordinary. It suggests that an event, situation, or fact is so remarkable or impressive that it is difficult to accept or comprehend.
    • Example: The acrobat's incredible performance left the audience in awe.
  • Improbable: This word refers to something that is unlikely or not probable. It suggests that an event or outcome has a low chance of happening or is not expected to occur.
    • Example: It is highly improbable for a novice chess player to defeat a grandmaster.
  • Out of the given options, the word that aligns with the meaning "that which cannot be satisfied" is "insatiable."
  • Hence option 3 is correct.

  •  "Deadly" directly describes the nature and effect of the gas released during the Bhopal gas tragedy. It implies that the gas was fatal or capable of causing death, which aligns with the historical accounts of the disaster where thousands of people lost their lives due to exposure.
  • "Abominable" refers to something that causes moral revulsion and is typically used to describe actions rather than the physical properties of substances. Therefore, it's less fitting in the context of describing a gas.
  • "Merciless" personifies the gas, suggesting it showed no pity, but it doesn't accurately convey the fatal nature of the exposure in the same direct way that "deadly" does.
  • "Incurable" is usually used to describe diseases or conditions that cannot be cured. While the effects of the gas might have led to incurable conditions, the term itself does not directly describe the nature of the gas as fatal.


Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2.'
